subject: Human Evolution
title: Toumaï: The Oldest?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Toumaï: The Oldest?.

hook.text: In 2001, Michel Brunet found a battered skull in Chad's Djurab Desert—nearly 7 million years old.

buildup.text: Named Sahelanthropus tchadensis, nicknamed Toumaï ('hope of life'), it may be the oldest known hominin.

discovery.text: Its flat face and small canines look hominin, but the brain was chimp-sized—right at the split.

twist.text: Critics argue it might be an ape, not a hominin. A single specimen makes certainty impossible.

climax.text: Found in Chad, not East Africa, Toumaï challenged the theory that hominins evolved only in the Rift Valley.

punchline.text: The oldest face in the family album is blurry.

quiz.question: Why is Toumaï controversial?
options: It may be an ape rather than a hominin
It was found outside of Earth
